text: 人不可貌相，海水不可斗量
pinyin: rén bù kě mào xiàng, hǎi shuǐ bù kě dǒu liáng
literal: person · not · can · judge by looks, sea · water · not · can · measure by dou
natural: Don't judge a person by looks; you can't measure the sea with a measure

meaning.en: A person's talent can't be judged by appearance, just as the sea can't be measured by the bushel.
meaning.zh: 不能凭外貌判断一个人的才能，就像海水不能用斗来量。

equivalents: Don't judge a book by its cover

examples.zh: 他其貌不扬，却是公司的技术骨干，真是人不可貌相，海水不可斗量。
examples.en: He's plain-looking but is the company's top engineer; you really can't judge a book by its cover.

examples.zh: 人不可貌相，海水不可斗量，别小看这个年轻人。
examples.en: Don't underestimate this young man; appearances can be deceiving.

usage.en: Often shortened to 人不可貌相. 斗 here is dǒu, a dry measure.
usage.zh: 常简称“人不可貌相”。斗是量米的器具。

pinyin: rén pà chū míng zhū pà zhuàng
literal: person · fear · become famous · pig · fear · fat
natural: People fear fame as pigs fear getting fat

meaning.en: Fame attracts trouble, just as a fat pig is the first to be slaughtered.
meaning.zh: 名声大了容易招来麻烦，就像猪长肥了要挨宰。

equivalents: The higher the monkey climbs, the more he shows his tail

examples.zh: 人怕出名猪怕壮，成了名人以后，他的生活再也不得安宁。
examples.en: Fame brings trouble; since he became a celebrity his life has had no peace.

examples.zh: 人怕出名猪怕壮，低调一点反而安全。
examples.en: Tall poppies get cut down; keeping a low profile is safer.

usage.en: Common in comments about celebrities and success; sometimes self-deprecating.
usage.zh: 多用于议论名人、成功者招惹是非，有时用于自谦。

pinyin: huā wú bǎi rì hóng
literal: flower · no · hundred · day · red
natural: No flower stays red for a hundred days

meaning.en: Nothing good lasts forever; prosperity and glory fade.
meaning.zh: 花不会百日常开，比喻好景不长，盛况难以持久。

equivalents: All good things come to an end

examples.zh: 花无百日红，再风光的明星也有过气的一天。
examples.en: No flower blooms for ever; even the brightest star fades one day.

examples.zh: 人无千日好，花无百日红，别指望一直顺利。
examples.en: Neither people nor flowers stay fine for ever; don't expect it to go smoothly always.

usage.en: Often paired with 人无千日好 and used as a reminder to stay humble.
usage.zh: 常与“人无千日好”连用，提醒人保持谦逊。

pinyin: tù zi bù chī wō biān cǎo
literal: rabbit · not · eat · burrow · side · grass
natural: A rabbit doesn't eat the grass beside its own burrow

meaning.en: A decent person doesn't prey on neighbours or those close to them.
meaning.zh: 兔子不吃自己窝旁边的草，比喻坏人也不在家门口做坏事。

equivalents: Don't bite the hand that feeds you

examples.zh: 兔子不吃窝边草，他再缺钱也不会向邻居下手。
examples.en: Even in need of money he'd never take advantage of his neighbours.

examples.zh: 兔子不吃窝边草，更别说人了，你怎么能骗自己的朋友？
examples.en: Even a rabbit doesn't eat the grass by its own burrow; how can you cheat your own friend?

usage.en: Can be a compliment (restraint) or an observation about not harming one's own area. Casual.
usage.zh: 可作赞语，也可说明不坑害身边的人。口语。

pinyin: yī cùn guāng yīn yī cùn jīn
variants: 一寸光阴一寸金，寸金难买寸光阴
literal: one · inch · time · one · inch · gold
natural: An inch of time is an inch of gold

meaning.en: Time is as precious as gold, so don't waste it.
meaning.zh: 时间像黄金一样宝贵，要珍惜。

examples.zh: 一寸光阴一寸金，寸金难买寸光阴，同学们要抓紧时间学习。
examples.en: Time is gold, and gold can't buy back time; students should make the most of it.

examples.zh: 一寸光阴一寸金，别再把时间浪费在游戏上了。
examples.en: Time is precious; stop wasting it on games.

usage.en: Common in school and workplace advice. Usually paired with 寸金难买寸光阴.
usage.zh: 常用于劝勉珍惜时间，多与“寸金难买寸光阴”连用。

synonyms: 花有重开日，人无再少年

pinyin: ér xíng qiān lǐ mǔ dān yōu
literal: son · travel · thousand · li · mother · worry
natural: When a son travels a thousand li, his mother worries

meaning.en: A mother always worries about a child who is far from home.
meaning.zh: 孩子出远门，母亲时刻挂念担心。

equivalents: A mother's worries follow her child wherever he goes

examples.zh: 儿行千里母担忧，出门在外要记得给妈妈报平安。
examples.en: A mother worries when her child is far away, so remember to tell Mum you've arrived safely.

examples.zh: 他出国留学，妈妈儿行千里母担忧，天天要视频。
examples.en: With him studying abroad, his mother worries so much she video-calls every day.

usage.en: Said with feeling about parents and children apart; often paired with the ironic reply 母行千里儿不愁.
usage.zh: 用于感叹父母牵挂远行的孩子，常与调侃的“母行千里儿不愁”对举。

pinyin: yī rì fū qī bǎi rì ēn
literal: one · day · husband · wife · hundred · day · kindness
natural: One day as husband and wife, a hundred days of affection

meaning.en: Even a short marriage creates deep bonds of affection.
meaning.zh: 做过一天夫妻，就有百日的恩情。

examples.zh: 一日夫妻百日恩，你们好聚好散，别把关系闹僵。
examples.en: A short marriage leaves a deep bond; part on good terms and don't turn it into a feud.

examples.zh: 一日夫妻百日恩，他离婚后仍然照顾前妻。
examples.en: Having been married, he still looked after his ex-wife after the divorce.

usage.en: Typically said of couples breaking up or old spouses; warm, slightly traditional.
usage.zh: 多用于劝说夫妻好聚好散，带传统色彩。

text: 千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重
pinyin: qiān lǐ sòng é máo, lǐ qīng qíng yì zhòng
variants: 千里送鹅毛，礼轻人意重
礼轻人意重，千里送鹅毛
literal: thousand · li · send · goose · feather, gift · light · feeling · heavy
natural: Sending a goose feather a thousand li, the gift is light but the feeling heavy

meaning.en: A small gift can carry great affection, especially when brought from far away.
meaning.zh: 礼物虽轻，情意深重。

examples.zh: 千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重，这点土特产请您收下。
examples.en: It's a small gift but comes with a big heart; please accept these local specialities.

examples.zh: 千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重，他特地从老家带了一袋米给我。
examples.en: It's the thought that counts; he brought me a bag of rice all the way from his hometown.

usage.en: Polite phrase when offering a modest gift; often shortened to the second half.
usage.zh: 送礼时的客套话，常只说后半。

pinyin: shòu sǐ de luò tuo bǐ mǎ dà
literal: thin · dead · 's · camel · than · horse · big
natural: A starved camel is still bigger than a horse

meaning.en: A once-great person or organisation still has more resources than ordinary ones.
meaning.zh: 大的东西即使衰落了，仍然比小的强。

equivalents: A great man even in ruins is greater than lesser ones

examples.zh: 别看他家破产了，瘦死的骆驼比马大，还有不少人脉。
examples.en: He may have gone bust, but a skinny camel is still bigger than a horse; he has plenty of contacts left.

examples.zh: 这家老牌企业虽然在走下坡路，但瘦死的骆驼比马大。
examples.en: The old firm is declining, yet it is still stronger than most.

usage.en: Neutral observation, often a warning not to underestimate a fallen power.
usage.zh: 多用于提醒不要小看衰落的大户。

pinyin: xīn jí chī bù liǎo rè dòu fu
literal: heart · anxious · eat · cannot · hot · tofu
natural: An impatient person can't eat hot tofu

meaning.en: Haste spoils things; some things have to be done patiently.
meaning.zh: 心里着急就吃不了热豆腐，比喻做事不能急躁。

examples.zh: 心急吃不了热豆腐，学习要一步一步来。
examples.en: Haste makes waste; study step by step.

examples.zh: 心急吃不了热豆腐，这件事得慢慢谈。
examples.en: Patience is needed; this has to be negotiated slowly.

usage.en: Advice to be patient, often said to someone hurrying.
usage.zh: 劝人不要着急，多对急性子说。

text: 踏破铁鞋无觅处，得来全不费工夫
pinyin: tà pò tiě xié wú mì chù, dé lái quán bù fèi gōng fū
literal: tread · broken · iron · shoes · no · seek · place, get · come · completely · not · cost · effort
natural: After wearing out iron shoes with no luck, it comes with no effort

meaning.en: After searching everywhere in vain, you find the thing by chance without any effort.
meaning.zh: 四处寻找没找到，却在不经意间毫不费力地得到。

equivalents: Look for something everywhere and find it right under your nose

examples.zh: 找了半年的资料，踏破铁鞋无觅处，得来全不费工夫，竟在旧书堆里发现了。
examples.en: After searching for half a year, I found the material in a pile of old books with no effort at all.

examples.zh: 踏破铁鞋无觅处，得来全不费工夫，丢失的钥匙原来就在口袋里。
examples.en: After searching high and low, the lost key was right in my pocket.

usage.en: Often quoted in full, but also shortened to 踏破铁鞋无觅处. Said with delight at a lucky find.
usage.zh: 常整句引用，有时只说上半句，表示意外之喜。

pinyin: shēn zài fú zhōng bù zhī fú
literal: body · in · fortune · inside · not · know · fortune
natural: Living in good fortune without knowing it

meaning.en: People often fail to appreciate their blessings while they have them.
meaning.zh: 生活在幸福之中却不懂得珍惜。

equivalents: You don't know what you've got till it's gone
Not knowing which side one's bread is buttered on

examples.zh: 你有这么好的工作还抱怨，真是身在福中不知福。
examples.en: You have such a good job and still complain; you don't know how lucky you are.

examples.zh: 孩子们身在福中不知福，哪里体会得到我们小时候的苦。
examples.en: Kids don't know how lucky they are and can't imagine our hardship growing up.

usage.en: Used in mild reproach; frequently addressed to someone complaining.
usage.zh: 多用于轻微责备，常对抱怨的人说。

pinyin: jiù jí bù jiù qióng
literal: relieve · emergency · not · relieve · poverty
natural: Help in an emergency, not poverty

meaning.en: You can help someone in an urgent crisis, but you can't support their poverty permanently.
meaning.zh: 可以帮人解燃眉之急，却无法长期救济贫困。

equivalents: Help a man in need, but don't keep him

examples.zh: 救急不救穷，借他一次钱可以，但不能一直接济。
examples.en: I'll help in an emergency, but I can't support him for ever, so I'll lend him money once.

examples.zh: 救急不救穷，真正的办法是帮他找份工作。
examples.en: Emergency help isn't a long-term solution; the real answer is to help him find a job.

usage.en: A reason given for limiting help; practical rather than cold.
usage.zh: 多用来说明帮助有限度。

pinyin: yǒu yuán qiān lǐ lái xiāng huì
literal: have · fate · thousand · li · come · meet
natural: With fate, people meet from a thousand li away

meaning.en: People destined to meet will find each other however far apart.
meaning.zh: 有缘分的人，即使相隔千里也能相遇。

equivalents: Those who are meant to be will meet

examples.zh: 有缘千里来相会，我们在异国他乡居然成了邻居。
examples.en: Fate brings people together over any distance; in a foreign land we became neighbours.

examples.zh: 有缘千里来相会，无缘对面不相逢。
examples.en: Those with fate meet from a thousand li away; those without pass each other by.

usage.en: Usually paired with 无缘对面不相逢. Said about friendship or romance.
usage.zh: 常与“无缘对面不相逢”连用，用于友情或爱情。

pinyin: qiú rén bù rú qiú jǐ
literal: ask · others · not · as good as · ask · oneself
natural: Asking others is not as good as asking yourself

meaning.en: Rely on yourself rather than depending on other people.
meaning.zh: 与其求别人帮助，不如依靠自己。

equivalents: God helps those who help themselves
If you want it done, do it yourself

examples.zh: 求人不如求己，有困难先想想自己怎么解决。
examples.en: Better to rely on yourself than ask others; think about how to solve problems yourself first.

examples.zh: 求人不如求己，他靠自己的努力考上了大学。
examples.en: Self-reliance beats begging favours; he got into university by his own efforts.

usage.en: Encourages self-reliance; common in motivational contexts.
usage.zh: 鼓励自力更生，多见于励志场合。

pinyin: yī rén zuò shì yī rén dāng
literal: one · person · do · thing · one · person · bear
natural: One person did it, one person takes the responsibility

meaning.en: Take full responsibility for your own actions without implicating others.
meaning.zh: 自己做的事自己承担，不连累别人。

equivalents: Own up to what you did

examples.zh: 一人做事一人当，这件事跟别人无关，由我负责。
examples.en: I did it, I'll take the blame; it has nothing to do with anyone else.

examples.zh: 他说一人做事一人当，主动承认了错误。
examples.en: He said he would accept all responsibility and owned up to his mistake.

usage.en: A bold, honourable declaration; common in stories and everyday speech.
usage.zh: 表示敢作敢当，多见于故事和日常口语。

pinyin: qiáng lǐ kāi huā qiáng wài xiāng
literal: wall · inside · bloom · flower · wall · outside · fragrant
natural: A flower blooms inside the wall but is fragrant outside

meaning.en: Someone's talent is better appreciated by outsiders than by their own people.
meaning.zh: 墙里开的花，香气飘到墙外，比喻成就在外面比在本地更受欢迎。

equivalents: A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country

examples.zh: 这位作家在国内默默无闻，却在国外大受欢迎，真是墙里开花墙外香。
examples.en: The writer is unknown at home but popular abroad; truly the fragrance is better outside the wall.

examples.zh: 墙里开花墙外香，他的手艺在邻镇比在本村更有名。
examples.en: His craft is more famous in the next town than in his own village.

usage.en: Often used about artists, products or ideas recognised abroad first.
usage.zh: 多指人才、产品或思想先在外地被认可。

pinyin: yuān yǒu tóu, zhài yǒu zhǔ
literal: grievance · have · head, debt · have · owner
natural: Every grievance has its source and every debt its owner

meaning.en: Hold only the person responsible accountable, and don't blame the innocent.
meaning.zh: 冤仇有起因，债务有债主，应找真正的责任人，不要牵连无辜。

equivalents: Blame the one who is guilty

examples.zh: 冤有头，债有主，你找他算账，别为难我。
examples.en: Take it up with him, not me; the one who wronged you is the one responsible.

examples.zh: 冤有头，债有主，不要迁怒于无关的人。
examples.en: Pin the blame on the right person; don't vent your anger on bystanders.

usage.en: Often said to deflect blame or to demand fairness. Slightly formulaic; common in dramas.
usage.zh: 常用来推脱责任或要求公平，戏剧中常见。

pinyin: bù pà yī wàn, jiù pà wàn yī
literal: not · fear · ten thousand, only · fear · one in ten thousand
natural: Don't fear the ten-thousand; fear the one

meaning.en: It's not the likely risk but the unlikely accident that causes trouble, so be prepared.
meaning.zh: 不怕出事的可能性大，就怕那万分之一的意外发生，所以要提前防范。

equivalents: Hope for the best, prepare for the worst

examples.zh: 不怕一万，就怕万一，出门还是把伞带上吧。
examples.en: Better safe than sorry; take an umbrella with you.

examples.zh: 不怕一万，就怕万一，重要文件一定要备份。
examples.en: Back up important files; it's the one-in-ten-thousand chance that hurts.

usage.en: Used to justify precautions; pinyin 万一 is wàn yī, a noun for 'the unlikely event'.
usage.zh: 用来强调防范，万一指意外的情况。

pinyin: ér sūn zì yǒu ér sūn fú
literal: sons · grandsons · naturally · have · sons · grandsons · fortune
natural: Children and grandchildren have their own fortune

meaning.en: Let the younger generation make their own way; parents needn't worry excessively.
meaning.zh: 后辈有自己的命运，长辈不必过度操心。

equivalents: Let the kids make their own way

examples.zh: 儿孙自有儿孙福，别替孩子安排一切了。
examples.en: The next generation will make its own fortune; stop arranging everything for the kids.

examples.zh: 奶奶说儿孙自有儿孙福，不再催他结婚了。
examples.en: Grandma says the young must find their own way, and has stopped pushing him to marry.

usage.en: Typically said by older people, resigned or philosophical; sometimes an excuse to stop worrying.
usage.zh: 多为长辈所说，带豁达或无奈。

pinyin: yī wù xiáng yī wù
literal: one · thing · subdue · one · thing
natural: One thing subdues another

meaning.en: Everything has something that keeps it in check.
meaning.zh: 每种事物都有制服它的另一种事物。

equivalents: There's always someone who can handle you

examples.zh: 老虎怕什么？一物降一物，它也怕火。
examples.en: Even tigers fear something; everything has its master, and a tiger fears fire.

examples.zh: 他在公司一向强势，在女儿面前却服服帖帖，真是一物降一物。
examples.en: He's domineering at work but meek before his daughter; every strong man meets his match.

usage.en: Often humorous, e.g. about a tough person yielding to a child or partner. 降 is read xiáng.
usage.zh: 常带幽默色彩。降读xiáng，意为制服。

synonyms: 卤水点豆腐——一物降一物
石膏点豆腐——一物降一物

pinyin: shào nián fū qī lǎo lái bàn
literal: young · years · husband · wife · old · age · companion
natural: Husband and wife in youth become companions in old age

meaning.en: A couple who marry young become each other's support in old age.
meaning.zh: 年轻时结为夫妻，到老了互相陪伴。

examples.zh: 少年夫妻老来伴，爷爷奶奶几十年来相互扶持。
examples.en: Young couples become old companions; my grandparents have supported each other for decades.

examples.zh: 少年夫妻老来伴，他们结婚五十周年了还手牵手散步。
examples.en: Husband and wife through the years, they still walk hand in hand fifty years on.

usage.en: Warm; often about elderly couples. The word 伴 here means 'companion'.
usage.zh: 温馨语，多指老年夫妻相伴。

pinyin: rén qióng zhì bù duǎn
literal: person · poor · ambition · not · short
natural: Poor but not short of ambition

meaning.en: Poverty doesn't diminish one's integrity and aspirations.
meaning.zh: 人虽然穷，志气和骨气不能丢。

examples.zh: 我们家虽然穷，但人穷志不短，从不占别人便宜。
examples.en: We are poor, but we keep our integrity and never take advantage of others.

examples.zh: 人穷志不短，他靠勤工俭学读完了大学。
examples.en: Poor but determined, he worked his way through university.

usage.en: Often paired with 马瘦毛长. Expresses dignity in hardship.
usage.zh: 常与“马瘦毛长”对举，表示贫穷而有骨气。

pinyin: lǎo shǔ guò jiē, rén rén hǎn dǎ
literal: mouse · cross · street, everyone · shout · hit
natural: A rat crossing the street, everyone yells to hit it

meaning.en: A hated wrongdoer is despised and attacked by everyone.
meaning.zh: 害人者人人痛恨，大家都要打击他。

examples.zh: 贪官污吏如同老鼠过街，人人喊打。
examples.en: Corrupt officials are like rats in the street; everyone wants to hit them.

examples.zh: 这种骗子老鼠过街，人人喊打，早晚没有立足之地。
examples.en: Such conmen are despised by all and will soon have no place to stand.

usage.en: Used for universally hated people or practices; derogatory.
usage.zh: 多指为众人所憎恨的坏人坏事，含贬义。

pinyin: jiāng hái shì lǎo de là
literal: ginger · still · is · old · one · spicy
natural: Old ginger is still the spiciest

meaning.en: Older people are more experienced and skilled.
meaning.zh: 老的生姜更辣，比喻年长的人经验丰富，办法多。

examples.zh: 年轻人冲劲足，但还是姜还是老的辣，关键时刻得请老师傅出马。
examples.en: Young people have drive, but ginger is always spiciest when old; in a crunch we need the old master.

examples.zh: 这场谈判姜还是老的辣，老张几句话就搞定了。
examples.en: In this negotiation experience told; Lao Zhang settled it in a few words.

usage.en: Often a compliment to an experienced person; can be said teasingly. Variant: 姜是老的辣.
usage.zh: 多用来夸奖老练的人，也可打趣。

synonyms: 不听老人言，吃亏在眼前
